title: TOEFL Writing Lab
sourcePolicy: 提供された非公開のTOEFL-writing.pdf全139ページを索引化し、全演習を移行。原PDF・スキャン・未整形OCR・個人の手書き答案は公開しません。原本の不備を校訂した設問は理由を表示。診断の並べ替え10問と掲載例2問は印刷解答と照合し、その他の正答・作文例・解説は根拠付きの編集作成です。作文の人物・日程補足は架空の練習設定で、公式採点ではありません。

exercises.title: 研修後の質問 · 間接疑問
exercises.prompt: Were there any questions during the training session?
exercises.modelAnswer: The new employees wanted to know if they would be able to access the system.
explanation: After wanted to know, use if + subject + verb, not question inversion. Would be able to takes the base verb access, which directly takes the object the system.
wanted to know の後は if + 主語 + 動詞の間接疑問。疑問文の語順 would they にはしません。
would be able to + 動詞の原形で「〜できるだろう」。access は他動詞なので access the system と続きます。accessing はこの to 不定詞の位置には入りません。
phrases: be able to access … — 〜にアクセスできる
want to know if … — 〜かどうか知りたい
exercises.answerBasis: 教材のSample Answers（PDF 16ページ）と照合済み。日本語解説は編集作成。

exercises.title: 展示の紹介 · 関係代名詞
exercises.prompt: Which exhibit do you recommend?
exercises.modelAnswer: A museum launched one last month that displays lots of fascinating artifacts.
explanation: One refers back to the exhibit, and the relative clause describes that exhibit. Because one is singular, the verb is displays; fascinating modifies the plural noun artifacts.
one は前の exhibit を受ける代名詞。「博物館が先月始めた展示」を that 以下で説明しています。
関係節の主語 that は単数の one を指すので displays。lots of + 形容詞 + 複数名詞の順で lots of fascinating artifacts です。
phrases: launch an exhibit — 展示を始める
fascinating artifacts — 興味深い遺物
exercises.answerBasis: 教材のSample Answers（PDF 16ページ）と照合済み。日本語解説は編集作成。

exercises.title: 遅延の相談 · 現在完了の疑問文
exercises.prompt: My group still hasn’t finished the project.
exercises.modelAnswer: Have you talked to your professor about the delay?
explanation: Use have + subject + past participle for a present-perfect question. Talk to identifies the person, while about introduces the topic of the conversation.
Have + 主語 + 過去分詞で、これまでに相談したかを尋ねます。talk は原形なので have の後の本動詞としては使えません。
talk to 人 about 内容。「誰に」と「何について」を取り違えないようにします。
phrases: talk to … about … — 〜に〜について話す
the delay — 遅れ・遅延
exercises.answerBasis: 教材のSample Answers（PDF 16ページ）と照合済み。日本語解説は編集作成。

exercises.title: 転職の理由 · 関係節の主語と動詞
exercises.prompt: Can I ask why you left your former job?
exercises.modelAnswer: I am looking for a position that better fits my long-term goals.
explanation: That refers to a position and acts as the subject of its relative clause. The singular antecedent requires fits; better modifies how the position fits the speaker's goals.
I am looking for … は「今、〜を探している」。a position の後の that が関係節の主語です。
that の先行詞 a position は単数なので fits。better は fits を修飾します。my は long-term goals の前に置きます。
phrases: look for a position — 職を探す
fit my long-term goals — 長期的な目標に合う
exercises.answerBasis: 教材のSample Answers（PDF 16ページ）と照合済み。日本語解説は編集作成。

exercises.title: 料理の進行状況 · 進行形の受動態
exercises.prompt: What did the waitress say about the order?
exercises.modelAnswer: She said the dishes are being prepared now.
explanation: The dishes receive the action, so use are being + prepared for an ongoing passive process. The present tense can remain after said when the reported situation still applies.
the dishes は調理される側。are being + 過去分詞で「今、調理されている最中」です。prepare は原形なので受動態の最後には使えません。
said の後で現在進行中の状態を報告する形です。現在も続く状況には are を使え、この教材の解答も are being prepared です。
phrases: be being prepared — 準備・調理されている最中
say (that) … — 〜と述べる
exercises.answerBasis: 教材のSample Answers（PDF 16ページ）と照合済み。日本語解説は編集作成。

exercises.title: 資料の送付 · would like 人 to
exercises.prompt: Your report last week was very detailed.
exercises.modelAnswer: Would you like me to email you the file?
explanation: Would you like me to introduces a polite offer: me is the object of like, and to email is the infinitive. Email you the file uses an indirect object followed by a direct object.
Would you like me to …? で「私が〜しましょうか」。like の目的語 me の後に to email が続きます。
email you the file は「あなたにそのファイルをメールで送る」。印刷済みの主語 you と語群の目的語 you は別の位置です。
phrases: Would you like me to …? — 私が〜しましょうか
email someone a file — 人にファイルをメールで送る
exercises.answerBasis: 教材のSample Answers（PDF 16ページ）と照合済み。日本語解説は編集作成。

exercises.title: 自転車の盗難 · while と受動態
exercises.prompt: Why did you decide to get a new bike?
exercises.modelAnswer: Someone stole mine while it was parked in front of the store.
explanation: Mine replaces my bike, while stole expresses the completed theft. It was parked is passive because the bike receives the parking action; the location follows in front of.
mine は my bike に相当する所有代名詞。stole は steal の過去形で、did を追加しません。
while 以下は it was parked（受動態）。in front of the store は駐輪していた場所を示します。
phrases: steal / stole / stolen — 盗む（活用）
in front of … — 〜の前に
exercises.answerBasis: 教材のSample Answers（PDF 16ページ）と照合済み。日本語解説は編集作成。

exercises.title: 課題の指示 · what が主語になる節
exercises.prompt: Why haven’t Harper and Bill started working on the assignment yet?
exercises.modelAnswer: They just learned what needs to be done.
explanation: What is the subject inside what needs to be done, so it needs no additional subject. Needs to be done combines a requirement with passive voice to identify the work.
learned の目的語は what needs to be done（何をする必要があるか）。what 自体がこの節の主語なので needs の前に別の主語は不要です。
need to be + 過去分詞は「〜される必要がある」。why では「何をするか」という返答になりません。
phrases: what needs to be done — する必要があること
just learned … — たった今〜を知った
exercises.answerBasis: 教材のSample Answers（PDF 16ページ）と照合済み。日本語解説は編集作成。

exercises.title: 売上計画 · 進行形と目的の不定詞
exercises.prompt: May I ask why you requested the sales data?
exercises.modelAnswer: My team is working on a plan to increase revenue over the next quarter.
explanation: Is working on expresses current involvement in a plan. To increase revenue explains the plan's purpose, while over the next quarter specifies the relevant period.
is working on a plan で「計画に取り組んでいる」。is と works を組み合わせることはできません。
to increase revenue は計画の目的・内容。over the next quarter は今後の四半期にわたる期間です。
phrases: work on a plan — 計画に取り組む
increase revenue — 収益を増やす
exercises.answerBasis: 教材のSample Answers（PDF 16ページ）と照合済み。日本語解説は編集作成。

exercises.title: 図書館に残った理由 · 関係節の受動態
exercises.prompt: Why did you stay late at the library?
exercises.modelAnswer: I was using some reference books that cannot be checked out.
explanation: Was using describes the activity in progress at that past moment. The relative clause cannot be checked out explains why these reference books had to remain in the library.
was using は過去のその時点での行動。some reference books を that 以下の関係節で説明します。
cannot be + 過去分詞の受動態で「貸し出せない」。check out は図書館の本を借り出す意味です。
phrases: reference books — 参考図書
check out a book — 本を借り出す
exercises.answerBasis: 教材のSample Answers（PDF 16ページ）と照合済み。日本語解説は編集作成。

exercises.title: 課題の送信確認
exercises.subject: Issue with assignment submission
exercises.context: You are taking an online course taught by Professor James through your university’s learning platform. Recently, you tried to submit an assignment, but an error occurred during the upload. Now, you are unsure whether the submission was successful.
requirements: Describe the issue you experienced.
Ask whether the assignment was submitted successfully.
Thank him for his assistance.
exercises.modelAnswer:
Dear Professor James,

I am a student in your online course, and I am writing about a problem with my assignment submission. When I tried to upload the file through the university’s learning platform, an error message appeared. I could not tell whether the platform had received my assignment.

Could you please confirm whether my submission was successful? If it was not received, I would be happy to upload it again or send it using another method you recommend. Thank you for your time and assistance. I appreciate your help in resolving this issue.

Best regards,
Sam Lee
explanation: Separate the failed confirmation from a proven delivery failure: the student does not yet know whether the professor received the file. Ask for confirmation politely, explain the technical problem, and thank the professor before offering to resend.
冒頭で受講生であることと送信トラブルの目的を提示。error message appeared → 受信が不明、という順に原因と困っている点を区別しています。
Could you please confirm whether …? は確認を頼む間接疑問。whether 以下を疑問文の語順にしません。未受信だった場合の再送案は、要求された3条件を満たした後の補足です。
「送信に失敗した」と断定すると、不明であるという設問と食い違います。最後に感謝を明示し、教授への丁寧な文体を保ちます。
phrases: I am writing about a problem with … — 〜の問題についてご連絡します
Could you please confirm whether …? — 〜かどうか確認していただけますか

exercises.title: 奨学金の金額訂正を依頼
exercises.subject: Urgent discrepancy on fee statement — scholarship amount
exercises.context: You are finalizing registration for the upcoming Spring semester. The scholarship amount on your online fee statement is $500 less than the official award letter you received three weeks ago. You need to resolve the discrepancy so that your tuition is paid correctly and on time.
requirements: Identify yourself, your student ID, and the semester of concern.
State the expected scholarship amount and the amount currently shown on your fee statement.
Mention that you have attached the original award letter for reference.
exercises.editorNote: 原本のTo欄はProfessor Jamesですが、設問本文の宛先Financial Aid Officeに訂正。名前・ID・未指定の金額は架空の情報で補ってください。解答例の$2,500と$2,000は編集例で、差額$500を保持しています。
exercises.modelAnswer:
Dear Financial Aid Office,

My name is Sam Lee, student ID S00001. I am writing about my scholarship for the upcoming Spring semester. The official award letter I received three weeks ago states that I was awarded $2,500, but my online fee statement currently shows only $2,000. The scholarship credit is therefore $500 lower than expected.

Could you please review this discrepancy and update my fee statement if an error has occurred? I need the correct balance to arrange my tuition payment on time. I have attached the original award letter for your reference. Thank you for your help.

Best regards,
Sam Lee
explanation: State the student's identifying details before comparing the expected $2,500 with the displayed $2,000. This makes the $500 shortfall clear; mention the attachment and request correction conditionally rather than assuming misconduct.
設問は氏名・学籍番号・学期を要求しているので、冒頭にまとめます。練習では架空のIDを使います。
expected $2,500 / shown $2,000 の比較で$500少ない状況を明示。「$500多い」と方向を逆にしないことが重要です。
添付した書類を I have attached … で明示。誤りと決めつけず if an error has occurred を添えて訂正を依頼するため、事務窓口への文体が適切です。
phrases: a discrepancy between A and B — AとBの不一致
I have attached … for your reference. — ご参照用に〜を添付しました

exercises.title: グループ会議の時間を変更
exercises.editorNote: 原本の最後の条件はcounter-の後がページ端で切れているため、提案した日時への投票、または別の案の提示を求める条件として整形しています。氏名と代替日時は架空の設定です。
exercises.subject: Change needed for Tuesday 6 PM group meeting — Marketing 301
exercises.context: You are part of a four-person team working on a major project for Marketing 301, taught by Professor Smith. Your team meets for two hours every Tuesday at 6:00 PM. Your required Statistics 205 tutorial has now been moved to Tuesday at 6:00 PM for the rest of the semester.
requirements: Explain the conflict caused by the required course change.
Propose at least two alternative days and times for the weekly two-hour meeting, and explain why they work for you.
Ask the team to vote on the proposed times or suggest another option.
exercises.modelAnswer:
Hi Alex, Jamie, and Kai,

My required Statistics 205 tutorial has been moved to Tuesdays at 6:00 PM for the rest of the semester, so I can no longer attend our Marketing 301 meeting at that time. I am sorry for the disruption.

Could we meet on Wednesdays from 6:00 to 8:00 PM or Thursdays from 4:00 to 6:00 PM instead? Both options allow us a full two hours, and I have no classes or other commitments during those periods. Please let me know which option you prefer. If neither works, could you suggest another time? Thank you for being flexible.

Best,
Sam
explanation: Explain the tutorial conflict, then give two complete two-hour alternatives with their advantages. End by inviting teammates to choose or suggest another time; this is a request to coordinate, not an announced decision.
変更の原因は必修tutorialの時間移動。自分の都合だけを曖昧に伝えず、元の火曜18時に参加できない理由を示します。
「曜日・開始・終了」を2案とも明示し、それぞれ2時間を確保。都合がよい理由も添えると第2条件を落としません。
チームメンバーにはHi … とBestで十分丁寧です。最後に好みを尋ね、代案も受け付けることで一方的な決定を避けます。
phrases: I can no longer attend … — もう〜に参加できません
If neither works, could you suggest …? — どちらも難しければ〜を提案できますか

exercises.title: レポート締切の延長を依頼
exercises.subject: Extension request: History 405 research paper
exercises.context: You are taking History 405: Modern World Conflicts with Professor Miller. Your major 15-page research paper is due this Friday at 5:00 PM. A documented family emergency required unexpected travel, costing you three days of work.
requirements: Identify yourself, the assignment, and the course.
Briefly explain the documented family emergency.
Propose a specific, reasonable new date and time.
Confirm that you will provide supporting documentation upon your return.
exercises.modelAnswer:
Dear Professor Miller,

I am Sam Lee from History 405: Modern World Conflicts. I am writing to request an extension for the 15-page research paper due this Friday at 5:00 PM. A documented family emergency required me to travel unexpectedly, and I lost three days that I had planned to spend working on the paper.

Would it be possible to submit the paper by Sunday at 8:00 PM instead? This would give me time to complete the remaining research and revise my draft carefully. I will provide supporting documentation when I return. Thank you for considering my request.

Sincerely,
Sam Lee
explanation: Identify the fifteen-page report and the original Friday 5 p.m. deadline. Ask for a specific new deadline, explain the three lost days without unnecessary private detail, and separately offer documentation after returning.
課題は15ページ、元の締切は金曜17時。提出対象と期限を冒頭で特定します。
緊急事情は必要な範囲だけ説明。家族の病名などを作り込みすぎず、3日失ったという設問の情報を使います。
Sunday at 8:00 PM のような明確な希望期限にし、延長が承認されたとは書きません。帰着後の証明書提出も独立した文で明示しています。
phrases: Would it be possible to …? — 〜することは可能でしょうか
supporting documentation — 裏付けとなる書類

exercises.title: 採点の再確認を丁寧に依頼
exercises.subject: Requesting re-evaluation
exercises.context: You are taking Political Science 310: Global Governance with Professor Chen. You received a C+ on the recent midterm essay. You believe you addressed the rubric and that a scoring error or misunderstanding of one main argument may have affected your grade.
requirements: Identify yourself, the assignment, and your current grade.
Politely explain why a re-evaluation may be warranted, referring to the rubric or a specific concern.
Ask for a brief office-hours meeting to discuss the paper.
exercises.modelAnswer:
Dear Professor Chen,

I am Sam Lee from Political Science 310: Global Governance. I recently received a C+ on the midterm essay and would appreciate an opportunity to discuss the feedback. I may have misunderstood the evaluation, but I believe my comparison of the two governance models addresses the rubric’s requirement to support the main argument with evidence.

Could you please review that section with me? I would be grateful for a brief meeting during your office hours so that I can understand whether my argument was unclear or whether a scoring error occurred. Thank you for your time and guidance.

Sincerely,
Sam Lee
explanation: Connect the request to a particular rubric criterion and the midterm essay, not merely a wish for a higher grade. Use tentative wording and ask for an office-hours discussion while allowing that your explanation may have been unclear.
成績C+とmidterm essayを明示。「もっと高い点が欲しい」だけでは再評価の理由になりません。
解答例の比較の内容は編集上の具体化です。ルーブリックの観点と自分の文章をつなぎ、may / I believe で断定的な非難を避けます。
office hoursで面談を求め、説明の不足だった可能性も認めると建設的です。採点ミスが確定したとは書かないようにします。
phrases: I would appreciate an opportunity to … — 〜する機会をいただければ幸いです
a scoring error — 採点上の誤り

exercises.title: 面接の再設定を依頼
exercises.subject: Rescheduling a job interview due to illness
exercises.context: You have a virtual final-round interview tomorrow at 10:00 AM for a Marketing Associate position at TechCorp. You woke up with the flu and do not feel able to perform well. You need to reschedule for later in the week.
requirements: Identify the position and the scheduled interview date and time.
Briefly explain the sudden illness professionally.
Propose two specific alternative days and times later in the week.
exercises.modelAnswer:
Dear Ms. Thompson,

I am writing about my final-round virtual interview for the Marketing Associate position at TechCorp, scheduled for tomorrow at 10:00 AM. Unfortunately, I have developed the flu and am not well enough to participate effectively. I apologize for the short notice.

Would it be possible to reschedule the interview for Thursday at 2:00 PM or Friday at 10:00 AM later this week? I am available at both times and would be happy to consider another option if necessary. I remain very interested in the position. Thank you for your understanding.

Best regards,
Sam Lee
explanation: Identify the role, company, and missed final interview before giving a brief apology. Offer two later alternatives and reaffirm interest; the suggested times are illustrative because the task does not fix today's date.
会社・職種・最終面接・元の日程を特定。症状の長い説明より、急な体調不良であることと短いお詫びが役立ちます。
新候補は木曜14時／金曜10時の2案。原本には具体的な曜日の現在地がないため、解答例は元の面接より後の候補という仮定で作成しています。
興味が変わらないことを1文で添え、採用側への敬意を保ちます。Mr.とMs.の両方を一つの呼びかけに書かず、練習上の設定を選びます。
phrases: I apologize for the short notice. — 急なご連絡で申し訳ありません
I remain very interested in … — 引き続き〜に強い関心があります

exercises.title: ボランティアのオファーを辞退
exercises.subject: Declining a volunteer position
exercises.context: Community Outreach Now (CON), a local nonprofit, offered you a volunteer Social Media Coordinator position. You recently accepted a paid part-time job that takes all your available time, so you must decline the volunteer role.
requirements: Express sincere gratitude for the offer.
Clearly and briefly explain that a new time commitment prevents you from accepting.
Reiterate support for the organization’s mission and wish them well.
exercises.modelAnswer:
Dear Ms. Rodriguez,

Thank you very much for offering me the volunteer Social Media Coordinator position at Community Outreach Now. I appreciate your confidence in me and was excited about the opportunity to support your work.

Unfortunately, I have recently accepted a paid part-time job that requires all of my available time, so I must decline the volunteer position. I would not want to accept a responsibility that I could not fulfill reliably. I continue to support CON’s mission of serving the local community and wish you and the team every success. Thank you again for your understanding.

Best regards,
Sam Lee
explanation: Thank the organization, clearly decline, and explain that the new job prevents you from meeting the commitment. Close with support for the mission without promising future participation that the task does not require.
感謝 → 明確な辞退 → 理由 → 応援、という構成。I must decline と書き、相手がまだ参加を期待する曖昧な文にしません。
就職先の情報を余分に書かず、時間を確保できないことを説明。「責任を果たせないまま引き受けたくない」で配慮を示しています。
団体のmissionを支持し、成功を願う文で結びます。未来の参加を約束する条件はないので、守れない約束を付け足す必要はありません。
phrases: I appreciate your confidence in me. — 信頼してくださり感謝します
fulfill a responsibility — 責任を果たす

exercises.title: 印刷物の誤配送・返金を依頼
exercises.subject: Formal complaint — incorrect order and late delivery — PF98765
exercises.context: You ordered a custom academic poster from PrintFast. It arrived after the promised deadline and was printed on glossy paper instead of the requested matte vinyl. The reflections make it hard to read under conference lighting. You want a full refund and an immediate replacement.
requirements: Identify the order number, promised deadline, and arrival date.
Explain both late delivery and the incorrect material.
Request a full refund AND an immediate replacement with the correct specifications.
exercises.editorNote: 注文番号PF98765は原本の件名に掲載。締切・到着日の具体的な日付は原本にないため、矛盾しない架空の日付で補ってください。
exercises.modelAnswer:
Dear PrintFast Customer Service,

I am writing about order PF98765 for an academic poster. Delivery was promised by September 10, but the poster did not arrive until September 12. In addition, it was printed on glossy paper rather than the matte vinyl specified in my order. The glossy surface reflects conference lighting and makes the text difficult to read.

I would like a full refund and an immediate replacement printed on matte vinyl using the original design. Please confirm when the replacement can be shipped and how the refund will be processed. Thank you for addressing these issues promptly.

Best regards,
Sam Lee

exercises.title: 国の理解：ニュースと映画
exercises.context: We have access to various forms of international media. Just by going online, we can watch news programs and movies from around the world. posts.text: News programs are more reliable. Movies often romanticize reality and change details, even when they are based on real events.

posts.text: Movies reveal ordinary life and cultural identity. News concentrates on exceptional events such as disasters, scandals, and crime, which can distort our image of a country.

For example, watching several films from different regions could reveal that a country has diverse traditions rather than one uniform culture. Derek is right that filmmakers change reality, so viewers should compare what they see with other sources. exercises.title: SNSはつながりか、孤立か
exercises.context: We live in a world saturated by digital platforms that claim to connect us. posts.text: Social media helps maintain relationships across geographical boundaries and find communities with specific interests or shared identities that may not exist locally.

posts.name: Sarah
posts.text: Many online connections are superficial. Platforms reward likes and validation, while constant comparison with curated highlights can cause inadequacy and isolation.

Repeated cooperation would create a genuine relationship rather than a temporary exchange of likes. Sarah is right that constant comparison can make users feel isolated, but this problem does not describe every use of the technology. Users can choose smaller groups and limit exposure to popularity metrics. Therefore, when platforms are used for shared activities and ongoing dialogue, their ability to build meaningful connections outweighs their tendency to encourage superficial interaction.

exercises.title: 代表民主制と直接民主制
exercises.context: Many modern democracies are representative, meaning citizens elect officials to make decisions on their behalf. However, some argue that with modern technology, we should move toward a more direct democracy, where citizens vote on every major policy issue. Which system provides a more stable and effective form of governance: Representative Democracy (elected officials making policy) or Direct Democracy (citizens voting on all policies)?

posts.name: Chen
posts.text: Representative democracy allows full-time expertise and deliberation. It can protect long-term interests and minority rights against impulsive majority decisions.

posts.name: Samuel
posts.text: Direct democracy reduces the distance between politicians and citizens, increases engagement, and makes policies reflect the public’s current preferences.

exercises.modelAnswer: Representative democracy is generally the more effective system because complex policies require sustained investigation and negotiation. I agree with Chen that elected officials can devote time to understanding issues that most citizens cannot study in depth every week. Consider a public transportation budget: voters may support lower fares without knowing how that choice affects maintenance or service frequency. Representatives can compare these costs, question specialists, and revise a proposal before approving it. Samuel’s concern about accountability is important, so citizens should still have accessible hearings and clear information about officials’ decisions. However, direct voting on every policy would not automatically provide the expertise needed for sound choices. A representative system with meaningful public oversight offers a more stable balance.
explanation: Support representative democracy through expertise and sustained deliberation. Develop the transit-budget trade-off, then respond to Samuel's accountability concern with public consultation and explanations rather than claiming representatives are always fair.

exercises.title: リモートワークと生産性
exercises.context: The shift toward remote and hybrid work models has dramatically changed workplace dynamics. Companies must decide if remote work is a net positive or negative for organizational goals. Does extensive remote work primarily increase employee productivity, satisfaction, and global talent recruitment, or does it fundamentally hinder team cohesion, innovation, and managerial oversight?

posts.text: Remote work removes draining commutes, allows employees to choose a productive environment, and expands recruitment beyond geographical limits. Employers can focus on output.

posts.name: Mark
posts.text: Extensive remote work weakens innovation and team cohesion by reducing spontaneous informal interactions and making communication more dependent on scheduled meetings.

exercises.title: 標準テストと教育の評価
exercises.context: Standardized tests are used widely to measure student achievement, school performance, and teacher effectiveness. However, they remain highly controversial. Are standardized tests primarily a fair and necessary tool for ensuring objective accountability and identifying achievement gaps, or are they an unreliable measure that promotes rote learning and exacerbates social inequities?

posts.name: Omar
posts.text: Comparable test data can reveal achievement gaps and systemic failures and help hold schools accountable for public funding.

posts.name: Jenna
posts.text: Tests may reflect preparation advantages and test-taking skills rather than deep understanding. Teaching to the test can narrow the curriculum and worsen inequality.

Students would then lose opportunities to evaluate evidence and explain their reasoning. Omar is right that comparable data can reveal achievement gaps, so I would retain tests as one diagnostic tool. Tests are useful evidence, but treating them as a complete measure risks distorting education.

exercises.title: 自動化と雇用・格差
exercises.context: The rise of AI and automation in the workplace is rapidly changing the nature of labor. Some see this as an opportunity for human flourishing, freeing us from drudgery. posts.text: Automation can increase productivity, create industries such as robotics maintenance, and move workers from repetitive or dangerous tasks into creative and interpersonal roles.

posts.name: Tanya
posts.text: The current wave also affects cognitive and service work. New jobs may require specialized skills, leaving displaced workers behind and concentrating wealth among technology owners.

exercises.title: 連邦と州：権限をどこに置くか
exercises.context: Federal systems of government divide power between a central (federal) authority and regional (state or provincial) governments. Giving both places the same detailed transportation policy could waste money without meeting residents’ needs. Regional authorities should be able to test different approaches and learn from one another. Jason’s concern about unequal rights is equally important, so national laws should establish protections that no region can weaken. Overall, decentralized implementation within a clear national framework offers the more responsive system.

exercises.title: 歴史の記念碑：称賛と文脈
exercises.context: Societies create public memorials (statues, monuments) to commemorate historical events and figures. There is frequent debate over whether these memorials should be purely celebratory or acknowledge complexities and flaws. Should public memorials primarily commemorate and celebrate a unified national narrative or hero to foster collective identity, or should they critique and contextualize historical figures and events to promote critical historical analysis?

posts.name: Rajiv
posts.text: Memorials should foster social cohesion and shared pride through a clear national narrative. Historical complexity can be studied in classrooms and museums.

posts.name: Erika
posts.text: Honest memorials should acknowledge injustice and complexity. Uncritical celebration can silence the experiences of people harmed by historical figures.

exercises.modelAnswer: I agree with Erika that public memorials should place historical figures in context rather than offer only praise. Public spaces are often where people first encounter a community’s history, so leaving out serious harms can create a misleading impression. For example, a monument to an industrial leader could explain both the jobs that the company created and the unsafe conditions workers faced. Visitors would then have a basis for discussing the person’s achievements and limitations. Rajiv is right that shared symbols can support social cohesion, but unity does not require ignoring disagreement. A concise plaque that presents multiple perspectives could invite more residents into the conversation. Acknowledging complexity can therefore strengthen a shared identity by making it more inclusive and historically informed.
explanation: Support contextualizing monuments rather than treating recognition as unconditional praise. The hypothetical example includes both achievement and harm; a short display with multiple perspectives adds a practical proposal to Rajiv's view.
contextualizeを支持し、公共空間が歴史に触れる入口であるという理由を追加しています。

exercises.title: 大学の文章課題と生成AI
exercises.context: The rapid accessibility of generative AI tools (like ChatGPT) presents a major challenge to traditional academic assignments, particularly essays and papers. Should universities strictly ban the use of generative AI in all assessed academic writing to ensure the integrity of individual student work, or should they integrate and teach the responsible use of AI as a mandatory tool for research and drafting?

posts.name: Sarah
posts.text: A strict ban protects independent thinking and the integrity of grading. Otherwise students could be rewarded for work they did not produce themselves.

posts.name: Leo
posts.text: Universities should teach responsible use and AI literacy, focusing assignments on synthesis, critique, and revision where human input adds value.

exercises.modelAnswer: Universities should integrate instruction in responsible AI use rather than impose a universal ban. I agree with Leo that students need to learn how to question and revise generated material, but Sarah is right that an assessment must still reveal the student’s own abilities. One solution is to require students to disclose how they used AI and submit notes showing the development of their argument. A teacher could also ask students to explain and defend their choices in a short conversation. These steps would make it harder to submit generated text without understanding it. Some assignments should remain AI-free to assess independent writing, while supervised AI exercises can be mandatory parts of instruction. This approach teaches useful skills without treating an AI-generated draft as evidence of individual achievement.
explanation: Support responsible AI instruction with disclosure, planning notes, and oral explanations. Respond to Sarah by retaining independent assignments that measure students' own ability, and develop Leo's AI-literacy point through concrete classroom rules.

学習用のAI演習と、独力の能力を測るAI-free課題を区別。AI文章を本人の成果として提出してよいという主張にはしません。

exercises.title: 高校生のボランティア必修化
exercises.context: Some high schools require students to complete volunteer hours before graduation. Should high school students be required to do volunteer work? Explain why or why not.

posts.name: Student 1
posts.text: Required volunteer work can build civic responsibility and show teenagers that their time and effort can improve other people's lives.

posts.name: Student 2
posts.text: Students already have limited time; some work part-time or care for siblings. A mandatory requirement could increase stress and make these responsibilities harder to balance.

requirements: Express your opinion and support it with reasons and a concrete example.

exercises.modelAnswer: I support a flexible volunteer requirement rather than a fixed number of hours for every student. Student 1 makes a useful point about learning civic responsibility, but Student 2 is right that students have different responsibilities outside school. A program should therefore offer several ways to contribute and reduce the required hours for students who work or provide family care. For example, a student could help at a community garden on a weekend, while another could organize donated books during a lunch break. Schools should also provide transportation or opportunities on campus, so volunteering does not depend on a family's income. With these safeguards, service can teach practical responsibility without unfairly increasing students' existing burdens.
explanation: The model takes a clear qualified position: a flexible requirement, rather than an identical rule for everyone. It responds to both civic benefits and unequal outside responsibilities.

exercises.title: 人文学の授業：古典と現代
exercises.context: Should university humanities curricula prioritize the historical canon, ensuring cultural literacy and intellectual rigor, or modern relevance, including diverse authors and contemporary issues that help students engage with today's society?

posts.name: Mia
posts.text: Classic works provide intellectual history, shared cultural references, and foundational debates needed for rigorous critical thinking. Ignoring the canon leaves students disconnected from the continuity of human ideas.

posts.name: Javier
posts.text: Students need diverse voices and current global issues such as climate change, racial justice, and digital life. Prioritizing a canon produced by a narrow demographic risks an irrelevant and exclusionary education.

requirements: Express your opinion and support it with reasons and a concrete example.
Make a meaningful contribution to the discussion in your own words.
Aim for at least 100 words.
exercises.modelAnswer: I would organize humanities courses around current questions while using classic texts to show how those questions developed. Javier is right that students should encounter diverse voices, but Mia's concern about losing intellectual history also matters. For example, a course about digital privacy could compare a historical argument about individual freedom with contemporary writing from different countries. Students would then examine which assumptions remain useful and which exclude important experiences. This approach gives classic works a clear purpose instead of treating them as a list that must be memorized. It also requires students to justify comparisons with evidence, maintaining academic rigor. Modern relevance and historical understanding can therefore reinforce each other when instructors design the connections carefully.
explanation: The position is more specific than study both: organize around contemporary questions and use classic texts to trace their development. The digital privacy example explains that structure.
Mia's rigor concern and Javier's diversity concern are both addressed. Evidence-based comparisons supply a mechanism for combining them, rather than assuming balance will automatically work.

exercises.title: 成績のインフレと評価の信頼性
exercises.context: Is grade inflation a positive adaptation reflecting improved teaching, student motivation, and competitive job markets, or a negative trend that reduces degree credibility and fails to distinguish students' abilities?

posts.name: Hannah
posts.text: Higher grades help students remain competitive when employers and graduate schools screen applicants by GPA. They may also reflect real improvements in teaching and learning resources.

posts.name: Ivan
posts.text: If almost everyone receives an A or B, grades lose their ability to distinguish excellent, average, and poor performance. That reduces the credibility of degrees and makes applicants' abilities harder to assess.

requirements: Express your opinion and support it with reasons and a concrete example.
Make a meaningful contribution to the discussion in your own words.
Aim for at least 100 words.
exercises.modelAnswer: I agree with Ivan that grades should communicate achievement clearly, but a rise in average grades does not by itself prove that standards have fallen. Hannah raises the important possibility that teaching has improved. Universities should therefore compare students' work against stable, published criteria before deciding whether higher grades are justified. For example, an instructor could use the same writing rubric across several years and ask another teacher to review a sample of essays. If the later essays genuinely meet more demanding criteria, higher grades are reasonable. If weaker work receives the same grade, the department should investigate. This approach protects students from arbitrary grade limits while preserving meaningful evidence of their abilities for employers and graduate programs.
explanation: The model separates rising grades from declining standards, avoiding the assumption that they are automatically the same. It then proposes stable criteria and independent sample review.
The conditional examples explain how evidence would distinguish genuine improvement from inflated grades. This adds an assessment method beyond the two students' competing claims.

exercises.title: グループ課題と公平な評価
exercises.context: Are group projects necessary for developing collaboration and professional skills, reflecting modern workplaces, or are they inequitable and demoralizing because contributions are often unequal?

posts.name: Leo
posts.text: Group projects let students practice managing conflict, delegating tasks, and holding teammates accountable in a realistic, low-stakes setting. These skills matter in many careers.

posts.name: Maria
posts.text: High-achieving students often carry teammates who contribute less to protect their own grades. A shared score can penalize diligent workers and reflect group dynamics rather than individual mastery.

requirements: Express your opinion and support it with reasons and a concrete example.
Make a meaningful contribution to the discussion in your own words.
Aim for at least 100 words.
exercises.modelAnswer: I agree with Leo that students need practice collaborating, but Maria identifies a serious problem with giving everyone the same grade. Group projects should combine a shared outcome with evidence of each student's contribution. For instance, a research team could submit one report, while each member provides a short explanation of the part they developed and the decisions they made. Brief progress meetings would also let the instructor identify unequal participation before the deadline. This is better than relying only on peer ratings, which can be affected by friendships or conflict. Students would still learn to coordinate tasks, but their final assessment would reflect both teamwork and individual understanding. Fairer grading can make collaboration more valuable rather than abandoning it entirely.
explanation: The model supports group work with a concrete condition: assess shared results and individual contributions. It directly answers Maria's objection without dismissing Leo's skills argument.
Individual explanations and progress meetings describe how the policy would work. The limitation of peer ratings adds a new reason for using more than one source of assessment evidence.

exercises.title: 全専攻にAIリテラシー教育は必要か
exercises.context: Should universities require every undergraduate, regardless of major, to complete a short course in AI literacy? Explain why or why not.

posts.name: Sofia
posts.text: AI tools already affect study and work. A shared course could teach students to check sources, recognize unreliable output, and use these tools responsibly instead of learning only by trial and error.

posts.name: Noah
posts.text: Degree programs are already crowded, and students in different majors use technology in very different ways. Departments should decide what training is relevant rather than adding another universal requirement.

requirements: State and support your position on a required AI-literacy course.
Respond meaningfully to both Sofia's and Noah's viewpoints.
Develop the response with a concrete example and at least 100 words.
exercises.modelAnswer: I support a short university-wide AI-literacy requirement, but it should include a common foundation and a subject-specific activity. Sofia is right that every student needs basic methods for checking sources, protecting private information, and recognizing confident but unsupported output. However, Noah's concern about crowded programs and different disciplinary needs is valid. Universities could limit the common course to a few focused sessions, then let departments design one applied assignment. For example, physics students might compare an AI-generated explanation with measured data and a textbook, while history students might trace quotations back to primary sources. This structure would avoid pretending that one tool is used identically in every field. It would also give all graduates a minimum safety standard without taking an entire semester away from their majors.
explanation: The response takes a qualified position: require a compact shared foundation, then adapt the application by discipline. This directly answers the professor instead of treating the two student posts as an either-or choice.

Sofia's reliability concern becomes three specific skills, while Noah's curriculum and relevance concerns shape the short format and departmental assignment. The physics and history examples show how one principle can be applied differently.
AI literacy は、AIの出力を鵜呑みにせず、根拠・個人情報・利用目的を判断する力です。unsupported output は「根拠のない出力」、primary source は「一次資料」。
このモデルは一つの論証例であり、公式スコアを示すものではありません。反対意見でも、両投稿へ応答し理由と具体例を展開すれば成立します。

exercises.title: 理系学生に口頭説明の訓練は必要か
exercises.context: Should science and engineering courses require students to explain calculations and experimental results aloud, in addition to submitting written work? Why or why not?

posts.name: Mina
posts.text: Oral explanation reveals whether students understand the reasoning behind a formula. It also prepares them to answer questions in research meetings and professional interviews.

posts.name: Daniel
posts.text: Speaking under pressure can disadvantage students who know the material but need more time or are still developing academic English. Written work is a fairer measure of technical knowledge.

guides.title: Eight word classes · 8品詞
items: Nouns name people, places, objects, or ideas. Common/proper describe naming; concrete/abstract describe whether the referent is tangible. 名詞は主語・目的語・補語になり、固有名詞は大文字で始めます。
Pronouns replace noun phrases and must match their referents. Use I/me, we/us, he/him, she/her, they/them according to grammatical position. 代名詞は指す対象と格・単複を一致させます。
Possessive determiners need a noun (my report); possessive pronouns stand alone (mine). Reflexives such as myself refer back to the subject. 所有格と所有代名詞を区別します。
Verbs express actions or states; auxiliaries build tense, questions, and negation. Modals such as can and must take the base form. 動詞・助動詞・法助動詞の役割を確認します。
Adjectives describe nouns; adverbs modify verbs, adjectives, or other adverbs. Careful work differs from work carefully. 形容詞は名詞、副詞は動詞などを修飾します。
Prepositions introduce relationships: in the room, to a colleague, about the deadline. Use an object pronoun after a preposition. 前置詞の後ろには目的格が来ます。
Conjunctions connect words or clauses. And adds, but contrasts, because gives a reason, although introduces a concession. 接続詞の意味と節のつながりを一致させます。
Interjections such as oh or wow express a reaction. Use them sparingly in formal writing. 間投詞は感情を表しますが、正式なメールでは文体に注意。

guides.title: Sentence constituents · 5文型
items: Identify subject (S), verb (V), object (O), complement (C), and modifier (M) before rearranging words. 主語・動詞・目的語・補語・修飾語を先に見つけます。
SV: He runs. SVC: He looks happy. The complement describes the subject; it is not an object receiving an action. 第2文型の補語は主語の状態を説明します。
SVO: He reads a book. SVOO: He gave me a book. The indirect object identifies the recipient. 第4文型では「誰に」「何を」の順。
SVOC: He considered the idea interesting. The object complement describes the object, so the idea is interesting. 第5文型では目的語と補語の意味関係を確認します。
Modifiers add place, time, or manner without changing the core pattern. Check verb use in context rather than assigning one permanent pattern to a verb. 修飾語を取り除いて文の骨格を確かめます。

guides.title: Determiners · 限定詞
items: A determiner comes before the noun and its adjectives: the two blue cars. It helps identify which thing or how much is meant. 限定詞は名詞句の先頭に置きます。
A/an introduces a nonspecific singular countable noun; the identifies a specific or shared referent. Choose a/an by sound, not spelling. 冠詞は特定性と発音で選びます。
This/that take singular nouns; these/those take plurals. Near/far may refer to time or ideas as well as physical distance. 指示詞の単複を名詞に合わせます。
My/your/his/her/its/our/their express possession before a noun. Do not combine an article with a possessive determiner: my book, not the my book. 所有限定詞に冠詞を重ねません。
Many/few typically modify countable plurals; much/little modify uncountable nouns. Some/any depend on meaning and sentence context. 可算・不可算を確認して数量詞を選びます。
Cardinal numbers give quantity; ordinal numbers give order. Enough indicates sufficiency, while no indicates absence. 基数・序数・数量詞の意味を区別します。

guides.title: Relative clauses · 関係節
items: A relative clause modifies a noun. Find its antecedent and the relative word's role inside the clause. 先行詞と、関係詞が節内で担う役割を確認します。
Who/whom refer to people; which often refers to things; that can introduce many restrictive clauses; whose marks possession. Whom is an object form. 人・物・所有の違いで選びます。
Where, when, and why introduce place, time, and reason relationships. They do not automatically replace a subject or object. 関係副詞と関係代名詞を区別します。
Restrictive clauses identify the referent and normally have no separating commas. Non-restrictive clauses add supplementary information and use commas. 制限用法と非制限用法は意味と句読法で判別。
Do not use that in a non-restrictive clause. An object relative may be omitted in a restrictive clause, but a subject relative may not. 非制限用法や主格では省略できません。
The exercises preserve the combined sentence's meaning and accept listed natural alternatives. Check subject–verb agreement with the antecedent. 関係節の動詞は先行詞の単複に合わせます。

guides.title: Active & passive voice · 能動態と受動態
items: Active voice makes the doer the subject; passive voice makes the receiver the subject. Use passive voice when the receiver or result deserves emphasis, or the agent is unknown. 何を主題にするかで態を選びます。
Build a passive with the appropriate form of be + past participle. Add by + agent when needed to preserve information. 受動態は be＋過去分詞。
Preserve tense and aspect: approved → was approved; is repairing → is being repaired; will display → will be displayed. 時制と進行中という意味を落としません。
When reversing a passive, make the by-phrase the active subject and return the receiver to object position. Check pronoun case: by us, but we finished. 格の変化にも注意。
The conversion exercises ask you to keep the agent and all details, even though an agent can often be omitted in ordinary writing. 練習では元の情報を保持する選択肢を選びます。

guides.title: Tense & aspect · 12の基本形
items: Simple forms: I work / I worked / I will work. Use them for habits, completed past events, or future reference as appropriate. 基本形は習慣・過去の完了・未来を表します。
Progressive forms: I am working / I was working / I will be working. They present an activity in progress at a reference time. 進行形は基準時点で進行中の動作。
Perfect forms: I have worked / I had worked / I will have worked. They connect an earlier event with a present, past, or future reference point. 完了形は前の出来事と基準時点を結びます。
Perfect progressive: I have been working / I had been working / I will have been working. They emphasize an activity's duration up to a reference point. 完了進行形は継続期間を強調。
For + duration differs from since + starting point. By + time often establishes the endpoint for a future-perfect construction. for は期間、since は開始、by は期限。
Time expressions help, but meaning and context determine tense. Finished past times normally require a past form; present perfect connects to now. 時間語だけで機械的に選ばず、基準時点を確認します。

guides.title: Email plan · 7 minutes
items: Identify the reader, relationship, and communicative purpose. Plan one short section for each required point. 誰に何を伝えるか、設問の条件を先に確認します。
Open with the purpose, give enough concrete detail, make the requested action explicit, and close courteously. 冒頭→必要情報→依頼→結びの順。
Use a tone suited to the relationship. Could you please confirm whether ...? requests information without assuming an error. 相手に合う丁寧さを選びます。
Allow time to check dates, amounts, names, and verb forms. Examples may invent reasonable logistics, but must keep every supplied condition. 原本の日時・金額・条件を変えません。

guides.title: Discussion plan · 10 minutes
items: Answer the professor's question with a clear position, then support it with a reason and a developed example. 立場→理由→具体例をつなぎます。
Respond to an existing idea and add your own contribution rather than merely copying or agreeing. 他の学生の意見に応答し、新しい内容を加えます。
Use at least 100 words as the task's practice target, with relevant detail rather than repetition. 100語以上を目安に、重複で語数を稼ぎません。
Qualify claims when necessary and distinguish hypothetical examples from established facts. 限定を加え、架空例を事実のように断定しません。

guides.title: Rubric · 評価基準の読み方
items: 5: The purpose or contribution is clear and developed, language is varied and precise, and errors are minor. 要件を十分に満たし、明確で発展した内容。
4: The response is generally effective, with adequate supporting detail, appropriate language, and few errors. おおむね伝わり、説明と語彙・文法が適切。
3: The response partly succeeds; missing or unclear development and noticeable errors can weaken the message. 一部の説明不足や誤りが内容を弱めます。
2: The response attempts the task, but limited development and language problems make parts hard to follow. 試みはあるが、内容や表現の制約が大きい。
1: Very little effective communication remains because ideas or language are severely limited. 意味のある内容や表現がごく限られます。
0: Blank, unrelated, non-English, or wholly copied responses do not provide an assessable answer. 空欄・無関係・英語でない・全体のコピーなど。
These task descriptors guide human review; they are not an automatic score or the section's official score. 語数やチェック数で点数を決めません。
